piece.caption: How to optimize AI model selection in Zapier to reduce automation task costs. Many business owners leave default Premium AI models running for simple data formatting steps, burning through Zapier task limits fast. AI by Zapier splits models into Standard (1 task), Advanced (3 tasks), and Premium (5 tasks). For bulk content, Gemini offers top performance at lower per-task costs, while GLM 5.2 costs just $0.22 per task for simple workflows. For tool-heavy steps, bringing your own API key (BYOK) cuts a 4-tool-call task from 25 tasks down to 5. Which AI model are you currently running in your Zapier zaps? Comment ZAPIER for the breakdown list.

material:
[68] Zapier Blog — Which AI models can you automate on Zapier? (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Moonshot AI, Z.ai, and more)
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/ai-models-on-zapier
Staying up to date on the latest AI models is like trying to keep my house vacuumed in the height of my dog's shedding season (a losing battle). New AI models drop practically every week, and it's not exactly obvious which ones deserve a spot in your workflows. This guide is your cheat sheet, with every model you can automate on Zapier right now, sorted by provider.
If you just want to cut to the chase and find out which model you should be using for which task, that's what AutomationBench is for. It's Zapier's own benchmark for how these models handle real, messy business workflows, so you can pick based on performance instead of hype.
Which AI models can you use with AI by Zapier?
Which AI models can you use on Zapier via direct integrations?
Bring your AI agent to the automation instead
There are two ways to bring AI models into your automated workflows: through Zapier's built-in AI step ( AI by Zapier ) or by using direct integrations with the provider.
AI by Zapier packages dozens of models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and more into one step, with no separate account or token billing—you just pay in Zapier tasks.
Direct integrations connect straight to a provider's own account instead, trading that simplicity for a wider lineup. Think legacy GPT or DeepSeek models, billed by token through your own API key.
Or, if you want to kick off workflows directly from your AI assistant, Zapier MCP lets you install Zapier in any MCP-compatible tool and start taking actions across 10,000+ tools straight from your chat window.
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 10,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Which AI models can you use with AI by Zapier?
An AI by Zapier step is your best option for adding AI into deterministic workflows . You get access to nearly 40 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai with no separate account and no token billing. Whichever model you choose, you get structured output fields, knowledge sources, agentic tool calling, prompt templates, and one-click model swapping.
You don't even need a separate account to use these models—they're built into Zapier, and you pay using Zapier tasks, not provider tokens. The models are sorted into task multiplier tiers based on the cost of the underlying model: Standard models use 1 task, Advanced models use 3 tasks, and Premium models use 5 tasks.
(If you prefer a model that isn't included by default, you can also bring your own key [BYOK] for a wider set of options inside AI by Zapier—more on that below.)
OpenAI models are the broadest lineup on Zapier, spanning everything from ultra-cheap classification models to frontier reasoning models. The breadth of the lineup makes OpenAI the safest default when you're not sure which model a workflow needs.
Best for: Coding and complex operations work
Claude is built to be careful and enterprise-safe, which is why companies like Slack, Notion, and Zoom have partnered with Anthropic directly. On Zapier's official AutomationBench leaderboard, Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic's top performer, ranking #7 overall at max effort ($4.64 per task), though you'll need your own API key to use it in AI by Zapier. Claude Sonnet 5.5 ranks #16 overall, at $1.14 per task. I recommend reaching for Claude when a workflow needs careful multi-step judgment, not just speed.
Gemini models offer some of the lowest per-task costs on Zapier—while still competing with the other state-of-the-art models on power. That makes Gemini the default choice when you're processing a lot of content and cost is the priority. Google's newest models hold the top five spots, and eight of the top ten, on Zapier's official AutomationBench leaderboard: Gemini 4 Neon takes #1, #2, and #4, and Gemini 4 Carbon takes #3 and #5. Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen also make the top ten, though Argon comes at a higher cost per task.
Kimi (from MoonshotAI) is a mixture-of-experts model purpose-built for tool use and multi-step agent tasks, priced well below most proprietary frontier models. Kimi K3 currently ranks #58 overall on Zapier's official AutomationBench leaderboard, at a fraction of the cost of most proprietary frontier models ($0.43 per task).
Z.ai's GLM family is priced well below proprietary frontier models, which makes it a solid pick for straightforward, lower-stakes automation. GLM 5.2 lands at #112 on the official AutomationBench leaderboard—behind Kimi and the frontier proprietary models—so it's a better fit for straightforward, lower-stakes automation than complex, multi-step work. At $0.22 per task, it's one of the cheapest options on the board either way.
Meta's Muse Spark and Wonder models are the Facebook parent company's response to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini.
DeepSeek is a cost-efficient open-weight model with strong coding and reasoning chops, popular for technical workflows on a budget.
Teams already running infrastructure in AWS often pick Bedrock so AI automation stays inside the security and compliance boundary their IT team has already vetted, with usage tracked under existing AWS access controls and spend commitments instead of a new vendor relationship.
Bedrock uses the AI models your company has already set up in Amazon Bedrock. The exact models depend on what's enabled in your AWS account and region.
Azure OpenAI is a common pick for regulated industries because it wraps the same underlying models in Microsoft's enterprise-grade security and compliance certifications, so your data stays inside your company's private Azure tenant instead of routing through a separate AI vendor.
Azure uses the AI models you've already set up in your own Azure OpenAI account. The exact models depend on what your Azure admin has turned on.
If you want to use a model that isn't built into AI by Zapier, you can also bring your own key (BYOK) for your preferred model. Models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google can all be used with BYOK—and some require it.
With BYOK, you'll use your own API key and pay the provider directly for tokens. If you don't know what that means, just pick one of the built-in models and move on. But if you're considering BYOK, these are the main benefits:
Cost control on tool-heavy workflows. BYOK runs at a 1x task multiplier even when a step makes multiple tool calls, compared to 3x on built-in Advanced models or 5x on built-in Premium models. A BYOK step with 4 tool calls would cost 5 Zapier tasks (1 for the BYOK, 1 for each tool call), while the same workflow on Premium would cost 25 (5 for the BYOK, 5 for each tool call).
Access to models that aren't in the default lineup, including newer models like GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.2, and Gemini 4 Argon, and legacy models like o3 and GPT-5.5.
